facts.t: Section 66A is still being used, a decade after it was struck down
facts.d: Shreya Singhal voided it in 2015 as vague and overbroad. Police stations kept registering cases under it for years afterwards, prompting the Supreme Court in 2021 to ask states to instruct every police station that the provision no longer exists.

facts.t: Sedition survived by changing its name
facts.d: The word sedition disappears from the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Section 152 replaces it — and widens it, covering subversive activities carried out by electronic or financial means, with punishment up to life imprisonment.

In the 1995 Cricket Association of Bengal case the Supreme Court held that airwaves are public property, not a government monopoly. That single holding opened Indian broadcasting to private television and led to the creation of an independent regulator.

bank.q: How many grounds of restriction on free speech are listed in Article 19(2)?
bank.e: Eight: sovereignty and integrity, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, and incitement to an offence.

bank.q: With reference to the right to protest, consider the following statements:
s: Ramlila Maidan (2012) recognised the right to protest as an implied fundamental right.
Amit Sahni (2020) upheld the right to protest but held there is no right to protest indefinitely in a public space.
T.K. Rangarajan (2003) recognised the right to strike as a fundamental right.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. T.K. Rangarajan held the exact opposite — there is no fundamental, and no statutory, right to strike.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (what it established about press and expression):
pairs: 1. Both qualitative and quantitative aspects of press freedom
bank.e: Thappar established freedom to publish, Sakal Papers freedom to propagate, Bennett Coleman the qualitative and quantitative dimensions, and Tata Press extended protection to commercial speech.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a right derived from Article 19(1)(a)?
o: The right to know, from State of UP v. Raj Narain
The right to silence, from Bijoe Emmanuel
The right to strike, from T.K. Rangarajan
The right to fly the national flag, from Naveen Jindal
bank.e: There is no derived right to strike — Rangarajan denied it. The other three are established derivations from the freedom of speech and expression.

bank.as: Section 69A of the IT Act was upheld in Shreya Singhal.
bank.rs: The Court read into it the safeguards of a reasoned order, a hearing and review by a committee.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The provision survived because of those safeguards — which is why the secrecy of Rule 16 and the absence of post-decisional hearings remain live grievances.

bank.q: Kedar Nath Singh (1962) narrowed sedition by holding that the offence requires:
o: Incitement to violence or a tendency to cause public disorder
Publication in a newspaper or broadcast
Proof of a conspiracy with a foreign power
bank.e: Only incitement to violence or a tendency to public disorder is seditious; mere criticism, however strong, is not. The Law Commission's 267th Report recommends embedding this test statutorily.

bank.q: Consider the following statements distinguishing hate speech from sedition:
s: Hate speech targets the dignity and equality of groups, a horizontal citizen-versus-citizen relationship.
Sedition targets sovereignty and security, a vertical citizen-versus-State relationship.
Hate speech has a single standalone statutory definition in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hate speech has no standalone definition — it is pieced together from sections 196, 197 and 299 of the BNS, and that vagueness is the core criticism.

bank.q: All of the following were held to be permissible restrictions or non-rights EXCEPT:
o: There is no fundamental right to trade in liquor — Khoday Distilleries
Crime cannot be a business — R.M.D. Chamarbaugwalla
A magistrate may prohibit all public meetings — Himat Lal K. Shah
Compulsory helmet rules are not a restriction on movement — Rajneesh Kapoor
bank.e: Himat Lal K. Shah held the opposite — the State may regulate the time, place and manner of assembly, but it cannot prohibit all public meetings.

bank.q: Which case struck down arbitrary internet shutdowns and required proportionality and periodic review?
bank.e: Anuradha Bhasin (2020), arising from the Jammu and Kashmir shutdown. Kaushal Kishore concerns speech restraints against non-State actors; PUCL concerns phone tapping.

bank.q: With reference to safe harbour under section 79 of the IT Act, consider the following:
s: Immunity is conditional on the intermediary acting as a passive conduit and observing due diligence.
Shreya Singhal read actual knowledge to mean a court or government order.
The IT Rules, 2021 define the word expeditiously with a fixed number of hours for all content.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Expeditiously remains undefined; the Rules prescribe specific timelines only for certain categories, which is why privatised over-removal is a persistent concern.

bank.q: Arrange the following speech judgments in correct chronological order:
bank.e: Kedar Nath Singh (1962) → Balwant Singh (1995) → Shreya Singhal (2015) → S. G. Vombatkere (2022), which kept section 124A in abeyance.

bank.as: The Bombay High Court struck down the Fact Check Unit under the IT Rules.
bank.rs: The scheme made the government the sole arbiter of what is fake news about itself.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the objection was structural, that no party can judge the truth of statements about itself, an argument central to Kunal Kamra's challenge.
